items.titleEn: Every word from Arteta's post-Liverpool presser
items.summaryEn: The manager on the big talking points from our 1-0 win
bodyEn: Mikel Arteta faced the media after our 1-0 win away to Liverpool on Sunday to discuss all the major talking points.
The boss was asked about the performance, the win, Christos Tzolis, restricting Liverpool to no shots on target and more.
Here’s a full transcript from his post-match press conference…

On whether it’s better to win here as a player or a manager…Now, it feels better as a manager because it's been such a long time without having this feeling here that we really needed it. We're extremely proud of what the team, the players, everybody has done. Especially in the condition that we arrived to this game, where we were after the defeat against Fleetwood, it looks like the end of the world. It looks like, yeah, what are we doing? Then you have to pick yourself up, understand that this is the beautiful part of this game. That's when you believe that you have done everything and deserve to win the game clearly, then you are out of a cup and then four days later you have to come to Anfield against this manager, against this team, that they are in a really good moment and compete, perform and earn the right to win the game in the manner that we've done.

On what securing a landmark win means for the players…Just loving the mission and the mission was something that we didn't accomplish in 14 years and there were reasons to that - some of them were psychological probably, some of them were related to the quality that we showed on the pitch, certain moments or decisions. We knew that we needed to nail absolutely all of them and we were going to have to navigate through periods that we were going to have to suffer because they are extremely good at doing that and creating those vertical attacks, those chaos moments for almost nothing. You really need to enjoy that. If you don't, there will be a moment that you will switch off and they will punish you. I think the way we competed and played and the chances that we generated as well, it was really impressive so I'm really happy.

On why he felt today was the day to beat Liverpool at Anfield…It was a feeling, how the hell can that happen? How can you get out of the cup when you shoot 27 times? We had the chances that we had against a team that had put one shot on target and then you look so silly. Then you have to go to Anfield and say, how can I lift those players up? I had a feeling and I said, now is the moment. We're going to have to dig deep, have an element of luck at times and for sure a lot of quality in the key moments and we've done it.

On Christos Tzolis’ performance…Again, it's the energy that he had in training. When I asked him the question how convinced he was, we had an issue with Ebs as well that it was incredible that he was in the squad today. I want to give credit to all the medical and the performance team because what they're doing with those boys is incredible, every three days to keep everybody at this level. That’s why these are the margins sometimes where you win a football match and not when you have somebody available or not. They deserve that credit and with Christos it's incredible. He didn't want to come off; he wanted to complete the game. We took some risks and at that point we decided, now is enough.

On triumphing at four grounds that we didn’t win at last season…That we have to do exactly what we did last season in the other grounds and then we know the results, but it's super early. I want to give credit to Liverpool as well in the manner that they played, the way they set up, to Andoni and what they are doing because they are a top side and it's very difficult. That's why I think winning here deserves even more credit.

On limiting Liverpool to zero shots on target at Anfield…I didn't know about that statistic but that's incredible. It didn't feel like this to be fair on the pitch because there were very little margins sometimes when they had the opportunity to shoot and it's a team that shoots a lot. You have to be so good at blocking shots and preventing those spaces for them to get into there. Again, it's a commitment of every single player in every action consistently to deliver those kind of stats and to do it against this team, it's something remarkable I would say.
On whether Liverpool deserved a penalty...I don't know, I haven't seen it. I will have to comment on a lot of actions that happened in the game otherwise.

items.titleZh: 阿尔特塔赛后新闻发布会全场采访
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳主帅阿尔特塔谈客场1比0击败利物浦的比赛。
bodyZh: 在周日客场1比0击败利物浦后，米克尔·阿尔特塔出席了媒体见面会，并讨论了所有主要话题。
老板被问及球队的表现、这场胜利、克里斯托斯·齐奥利斯、将利物浦的射正次数限制为零等等。
以下是他赛后新闻发布会的完整文字实录……

关于作为一名球员还是教练在这里赢球感觉更好……现在，感觉作为教练更好，因为我们已经很长时间没有在这里有过这种感觉了，我们真的很需要它。我们对球队、球员以及每个人所做的一切感到极其自豪。特别是在我们来到这场比赛的状况下，在我们输给弗利特伍德之后，看起来像是世界末日。看起来就像是，是的，我们在做什么？然后你必须振作起来，明白这是这项运动美丽的一部分。当你相信自己已经做了一切并且理应清楚地赢得比赛时，结果你却被淘汰出局了，四天后你又必须来到安field面对这位教练、这支球队，他们在状态极佳的时候竞争、表现，并以我们所做的方式赢得赢球的权利。

关于一场具有里程碑意义的胜利对球员意味着什么……只是热爱这个使命，而这个使命是我们14年来都没有完成的，这背后有原因——其中一些可能是心理原因，一些与我们在球场上表现出的质量、某些时刻或决定有关。我们知道我们需要把它们全部做好，我们将不得不度过一段我们不得不痛苦的时期，因为他们在做到这一点以及创造那些纵向进攻、几乎凭空制造混乱时刻方面非常出色。你真的需要享受这一点。如果你不这样做，就会有某一刻你分心，他们会惩罚你。我认为我们竞争和踢球的方式以及我们创造的机会也真的令人印象深刻，所以我真的很高兴。
关于为什么他觉得今天是击败利物浦的日子……这是一种感觉，这怎么可能发生？当你有27次射门时，你怎么会被淘汰出局？我们在对阵一支只有一次射正的球队时获得了机会，然后你看上去显得很傻。然后你必须去安菲尔德，说，我怎么能振作这些球员？我有一种感觉，我说，现在就是时刻。我们必须深入挖掘，有时带有一点运气，当然在关键时刻有很高的质量，我们做到了。

关于克里斯托斯·齐奥利斯的表现……再次强调，这是他在训练中的能量。当我问他他有多大信心时，我们还有一个问题，埃布斯今天能进大名单简直难以置信。我要感谢所有的医疗和表现团队，因为他们在这些男孩身上做的事情简直难以置信，每三天就能把每个人保持在这个水平。这就是为什么有时候这就是你赢得足球比赛而不是当你有人可用或不可用的差距。他们应得赞誉，对克里斯托斯来说这是不可思议的。他不想下场；他想踢完整场比赛。我们承担了一些风险，在那一刻我们决定，现在够了。
关于在过去一个赛季未能取胜的四个球场取得胜利……我们需要在其他球场上完全复制上赛季的做法，然后我们就知道结果了，但现在还为时过早。我也想赞扬利物浦的表现方式、他们的排兵布阵、安多尼以及他们正在做的事情，因为他们是一支顶级球队，这非常困难。这就是为什么我认为在这里赢球更值得称赞。
关于在安菲尔德将利物浦的射正次数限制为零……我不知道这个统计数据，但那太不可思议了。说实话，在球场上感觉并非如此，因为有时当他们有机会射门时，差距非常小，而且这是一支射门很多的球队。你必须非常擅长封堵射门并阻止他们进入这些空间。再说一次，这是每个球员在每个动作中始终如一的承诺，才能提供这种统计数据，并且对阵这支球队，我要说这非常了不起。
关于利物浦是否配得上点球……我不知道，我没看到。否则我将不得不对比赛中发生的大量动作发表评论。

items.summaryEn: Our midfielder on a monstrous bounce-back from midweek
bodyEn: Declan Rice put in another monumental shift to help guide us to a 1-0 win at Anfield on Sunday.
Our midfielder was named player-of-the-match after contributing the assist for our only goal, then covered every blade of grass as we saw out the win with a determined and tireless performance.
All the hard work was worth it, as we recorded our first league win at the venue since 2012, and went three points clear at the top of the table.
“Coming to Anfield, I think the record here speaks for itself - the first win here in 14 years - so today to win 1-0, to show that togetherness, resilience – it’s unbelievable.
“I’m just delighted to get the win and the three points.”

He revealed that Mikel Arteta’s pre-match team talk centered on ending our winless run at Anfield: “The manager drilled that into us, showed us the last time before we won at Spurs away, Chelsea away, it was many, many years, and Liverpool was the longest outstanding one. He drilled it into us to have that mentality to come here today and win, to show that togetherness.

“I think the togetherness is unmatched. I’ve never been in a team like it that’s got this togetherness. The manager, what he’s built, how happy everyone is every day to come in, see each other, work and represent this club - it’s amazing.”
On a personal note, Dec said he was proud of his own contribution, especially as it’s a venue where he hasn’t had much to celebrate previously.

“Yeah delighted because this Liverpool team has so much quality. I’ve been on the end of some big results here before, so to come and win today, put in a really good performance against a top side who are doing really, really well, I’m delighted.

“After Tuesday it felt like the world had come crashing down, losing to Fleetwood, but then to have the reaction like this - that’s the beauty of football. You always have one the week after to put things right, and we’ve done that today and made Arsenal fans very happy. So, bring on Wednesday.”

items.titleZh: 赖斯：这种团结精神是无与伦比的
items.summaryZh: 赖斯谈周中失利后的强势反弹及客胜安菲尔德。
bodyZh: 周日，德克兰·赖斯又一次奉献了卓越的表现，帮助我们在安菲尔德以1-0取胜。
这位中场球员被评为全场最佳球员，他为球队打入的唯一进球贡献了助攻，随后全场不知疲倦地奔跑，用坚决的表现守住了胜果。
所有的辛苦付出都是值得的，我们自2012年以来首次在联赛客场击败对手，并在积分榜上以三分优势领跑。
“来到安菲尔德，这里的纪录说明了一切——14年来首次在这里取胜——所以今天以1-0取胜，展现出这种团结和韧性，真是难以置信。”
“我很高兴能赢得比赛和三分。”
他透露，米克尔·阿尔特塔在赛前动员中重点强调了终结我们在安菲尔德不胜纪录的重要性：“主教练向我们灌输了这一点，向我们展示了我们客场击败热刺、切尔西之前已经过去了多少年，而利物浦是历时最长的一项。他向我们灌输了这种心态，让我们今天来到这里并赢得胜利，展现出那种团结。”
“我认为这种团结是无与伦比的。我从未效力过拥有如此团结精神的球队。主教练所建立的一切，每个人每天来这里、看到彼此、努力工作并代表这家俱乐部的快乐——这太棒了。”
谈到个人表现，赖斯表示他对自己的贡献感到自豪，特别是在这个他过去很少有美好回忆的球场。
“是的，我很高兴，因为这支利物浦队实力非常强劲。我以前在这里遭遇过一些惨败，所以今天能够赢球，在面对一支表现非常非常出色的顶尖球队时拿出精彩的表现，我很高兴。”
“周二输给弗利特伍德后，感觉世界仿佛要塌下来了，但随后能有这样的反应——这就是足球的魅力。你总能在接下来的一周迎来救赎的机会，我们今天做到了，让阿森纳球迷非常高兴。所以，迎接周三的比赛吧。”

items.titleEn: Arteta on a proud day for the club
items.summaryEn: The manager reflects on ending our winless run at Anfield
bodyEn: Mikel Arteta was on the pitch as a player the last time we won at Anfield, today he was in the dugout, overseeing our first win away to Liverpool since 2012.
The manager saw his team put in a determined and resilient performance to earn a 1-0 win, thanks to Kai Havertz’s first-half goal.
Afterwards the boss spoke about his pride for what his players had delivered throughout the 90 minutes.

“So happy, so proud, full of energy,” he said at full-time. “What can I say - it’s a proud moment for everybody attached with the football club. It’s been 14 years waiting for this moment, and we did it in very special circumstances after the defeat against Fleetwood in a way we didn’t deserve four days ago. And now having to come to Anfield, making sure everybody is convinced, prepared and ready to navigate a football match, that is going to have very difficult moments, some big opportunities and when they come, you need to be ready to grab them. What the boys have done is remarkable.”

There were top performances all over the pitch, and the defensive solidity was such that we became the first side to stop Liverpool from having a shot on target in a home Premier League match since Opta started recording the data in 2003/04. But the manager said it was an all-round performance, and also praised our attacking output.
“First of all, the quality in the top moments that you have to deliver to score the goals, to generate six, seven big chances like we’ve done.

“Then the resilience to go again, and again, again, against a team that can turn games into a very chaotic moment, with a lot of space, runners, a lot of fight, unbelievable with second balls, and they’re extremely good at that. To maintain the focus and the ability to consistently do that well throughout the game, it’s something that’s not easy at all to do.”

Arteta’s post-match demeanour was in stark contrast to Tuesday night, when we crashed out of the Carabao Cup to League Two side Fleetwood. He said a lot of the foundation for Sunday’s win was down to the hard work put in during the day’s leading up to our clash with Liverpool.

“The first thing was for myself to get up after the defeat against Fleetwood, because that was extremely painful. I know the club that we represent and when you are out of the cup in the manner that we have done it, it hurts a lot.

“But it’s a learning as well for me, because there’s no time to feel sorry for yourself, to start to dig into that - it’s football, we didn’t deserve to get out; we got out. Okay, let’s think why this happened, and now how I’m going to look into the eyes of the boys and start the next day, the next morning, and convince them that four days later we're going to come to Anfield. We’ve all had that feeling since Friday.”
The manager finished his interview with us by praising Christos Tzolis, who was a constant menace on the left wing, despite not featuring at all for the last month with a hamstring injury.

”Incredible. Big credit to the medical department, the sports science department, and the physios for what they’ve done with him. Obviously, his mentality and approach to every single day, the detail every single day to prepare himself, is just incredible.”

items.titleZh: 阿尔特塔：这是俱乐部令人自豪的一天
items.summaryZh: 主帅谈球队在安菲尔德终结不胜纪录。
bodyZh: 米克尔·阿尔特塔上一次作为球员在安菲尔德获胜时身披阿森纳战袍，今天他坐在教练席上，指挥球队取得了自2012年以来客场对阵利物浦的首场胜利。
凭借哈弗茨在上半场的进球，主帅看到他的球队展现出坚决和顽强的表现，赢得了1-0的胜利。
赛后，主帅谈到了他对球员们在90分钟内表现出的水准感到自豪。

“非常高兴，非常自豪，充满了活力，”他在终场哨响时说道。“我能说些什么呢——对于所有与这家足球俱乐部息息相关的人来说，这是一个令人自豪的时刻。我们等待这一刻已经14年了，在四天前以不应有的方式输给弗利特伍德之后，我们在非常特殊的情况下做到了这一点。现在来到安菲尔德，确保每个人都坚信、准备好并准备好驾驭一场比赛，这场比赛会有非常困难的时刻，有一些绝佳的机会，当它们到来时，你需要准备好抓住它们。小伙子们所做的是非凡的。”
全场各处都有顶级的发挥，防守的稳固性使我们成为自Opta自2003/04赛季开始记录数据以来，第一支在英超主场比赛中让利物浦没有射正的球队。但主帅表示这是一场全面的表现，并称赞了我们的进攻产出。
“首先，在关键时刻你必须展现出的高质量来进球，创造六、七次我们所做的那样的大好机会。”
“然后是面对一支能把比赛变成非常混乱局面的球队时，一次又一次地坚持下去的韧性，那里有很多空间、前插球员、大量的拼抢，在争抢第二落点时不可思议，他们在这方面极其出色。在整场比赛中保持注意力的集中和始终如一地做好这件事的能力，这绝非易事。”
阿尔特塔赛后的神态与周二晚上形成鲜明对比，当时我们在联赛杯中被英乙球队弗利特伍德淘汰出局。他表示，周日胜利的许多基础都要归功于在对阵利物浦的几天里所付出的艰苦努力。
“第一件事是我自己要在输给弗利特伍德后振作起来，因为那极其痛苦。我知道我们所代表的俱乐部，当你以我们那样的方式被淘汰出杯赛时，这非常令人心痛。”
“但这也是对我的一个教训，因为没有时间去自怨自艾，去深陷其中——这就是足球，我们不该出局；但我们出局了。好吧，让我们想想为什么会发生这种情况，以及接下来我将如何看着小伙子们眼睛，开始第二天，第二天早上，并说服他们四天后我们要去安菲尔德。从周五开始，我们大家都有了这种感觉。”
主帅在采访的最后称赞了克里斯托斯·特佐利斯，尽管他在过去一个月里因腿筋受伤没有出场，但在左翼依然构成了持续的威胁。
“不可思议。医疗部门、运动科学部门以及理疗师们为他所做的一切值得大加赞赏。显然，他的心态和对每一天的态度，每天为了准备好自己而关注的细节，简直不可思议。”

items.titleEn: Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal: Premier League – as it happened
items.summaryEn: Kai Havertz’s goal was enough to give Arsenal their first win at Anfield since September 2012 and take them three points clear at the top of the tableSo where is the game? Liverpool will look to get men around the ball when Arsenal have it, opening the pitch for switches should they win possession. And when they don’t, they’ll run like mad to recover it, stretching play and passing forwards, facilitating that by conserving energy every now and again when Nyoni slows the game down.In particular, I expect they’ll ask Bradley Barcola to target the space left when Riccardo Calafiori goes off on adventures, with Alexander Isak pulling away for cut-backs and shooting quickly with little backlift, while Florian Wirtz looks to slip passes in behind – if he can work quickly enough in the maelstrom of the match. Continue reading...
bodyEn: Aha, David Hytner’s match report is with us.
That means we’re finished here, so thanks for all your company and comments – sorry I couldn’t use them all – and peace out.

Van Dijk tells Sky Liverpool could’ve done more in the last 15 minutes but is disappointed. He thinks they played better after conceding, Mac Allister’s header could’ve changed the game, and he thinks it was a clear penalty on Isak.
Asked if Isak should’ve complained more, he says there are plenty of cameras, so well done to Arsenal.

When someone new comes in, he says, it needs time, work, going through difficult moments and so on. The fans can see there’s so much improvement already in recent weeks, they work their socks off, which is the bare minimum, especially at Liverpool, and what they need is results.

“Not forceful or violent” was VAR’s verdict on Madueke’s little nodlet on Mac Allister. I think that’s the correct call, but again, we need to do something with the laws; currently, we seem to have instituted a system whereby minor off-ball offences and general petulance are judged more harshly than tackles which can cause injury.
I guess Wirtz was signed to be that, but it doesn’t look like he can work quickly enough to compensate for his lack of power and explosive speed.
On the other hand, there are young players coming through who might change that – Max Dowman and Rio Ngumoha most particularly.

That game was, by the way, exactly why I said the Premier League lacks attacking quality. Watching two of the most expensively assembled teams in history, we saw very little in terms of wit, interplay and individual improvisation. The speed, intensity and physicality were something, but neither side had a player able to make sense of it all.
Also going on:
Declan Rice says Anfield creates waves of sustained attacks, but they got off to a good start and their togetherness is “undefeated … like nothing I’ve ever seen before”.

Haveertz says Liverpool have top players and can show their quality, but they stuck together, defended together, and there were tough moments. On the goal, he says 90% of it belongs to Rice – “we all know his right foot”.

Back to Rice, he says the manager “had a really honest conversation” with him at the start of the season, telling him he could do more, and before the game, he told Havertz to attack the box. It’s his first win at Anfield, but it doesn’t mean anything in terms of the table; you take it seriously in February and March. Before that, you just win as many games as you can.
Rice is given player of the match and, though I’d have gone for Gabriel, I can’t argue with that.

“They just fell short,” says Adam Darke, but the truth is Liverpool weren’t really close. Opta have just decided that Barcola shot does’t count as one, so they went 96 minutes at home without mustering one; they had the Mac Allister header over the bar and Wirtz’s free-kick that hit the bar, but pretty much nothing else.
Or, put another way, Iraola has work to do – but they won’t play teams who defend like Arsenal every week.

Arsenal win at Anfield for the first time since September 2012; Mikel Arteta wins at Arsenal for the first time in his managerial career. They move top of the table thanks to a colossal effort of collective organisation and defending; it’ll take something significant to stop them retaining their title.
90+6 min Szoboszlai moves it forward, Tsimikas’ attempted cross is blocked by Madueke, and when the ball is pumped back into the Arsenal box, Raya quickly gathers.
90+5 min Alisson punts downfield, Van Dijk makes first contact, and Isak is penalised for a foul on Gabriel. That will probably be it.
90+4 min Two more minutes and, if they don’t concede, Arsenal are going clear at the top. This has been a monstrous rearguard, even if they’ve not been confronted with much quality.
90+2 min Barcola trickles a shot that Raya fields easily; that’s their first one on target. Raya is booked shortly afterwards for wasting time.

90+1 min The corner is cleared so Liverpool come again, but they ran out of ideas some time ago;, if indeed they ever really had any beyond sticking balls into the box. They’v been decent up until that point, but I’m not sure why they’re constructing attacks exactly as Arsenal want them to.

90 min Another ball tossed into the box, Van Dijk flicks on, ands Munoz inhales to squeeze between Calafiori and Hincapie, but can’t get enough on his header. But Liverpool sustain the attack, Ngumoha’s cross blocked behind for a corner; we’ll have six additional minutes.

89 min Arteta sends on Merino for Odegaard, and this reminds me a little of the Bayern game last season, Arsenal securing victory by sending on athletes. They lack a little bit finesse, as Wenger might’ve said but playing them is no fun for anyone.
88 min I thoght Gyokeres might’ve come on earlier to run channels, and when Szoboszlai runs into Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly has a chance to hit him … but puts too much on the pass.

86 min This has been a disappointing second half from Liverpool. The link-up play around the box hasn’t been good enough, but also, they haven’t attempted enough of it. But here’s Ngumoha, running at Calafiori and tossing a few lollipops, his shot blocked out for a throw; Van Dijk is now playing centre-forward, so expect yet more crosses.
84 min Changes for Arsenal, Hincapie and Gyokeres for Tzolis and Havertz. Havertz isn’t everyone’s idea of a centre-forward, mine included, but his record in big games is superb.
82 min Ch ch changes for Liverpool, Munoz, who’ll play right-back, Koumas and Tsimikas on, with Araujo, Wirtz and Kerkez off.
81 min VAR makes the call to let things be; good. Mac Allister and Timber are both booked; the former should be ashamed of the show he made of himself.

79 min Mac Allister fouls Odegaard, then bends double to get in his face, applying a minor slap for extra aggravation. Naturally, sentiments are then exchanges, Timber to the fore, then Madueke puts a forehead next to Mac Aillster’s; I’m not sure there’s forward motion, but there is minor contact, Mac Allister goes down like he’s been deflated, and VAR has a decision to make.

77 min But in the meantime, Ngumoha comes in on his weaker foot, crossing to the back post, and when the ball is knocked back by Van Dijk, Araujo tries to muscle a shot but it bloicked off at source. Liverpool still haven’t had a shot on target which tells you plenty about Arsenal’s defending – and their lack of slickness when it really counts.

75 min Ngumoha conjures space down the right but can’t quite find a gap big enough to sneak through. I wonder if, at some point soon, Iraola might swap him with Barcola, who has the speed to get down the outside, so he can attack the diagonal angle towards the box.
74 min I meant to say, Lewis-Skelly was booked a few minutes ago for bouncing Isak.

73 min Arsenal are starting to control things and, as I type, Madueke moves down the left, sliding square to Tzolis on the other side. He opens the angle for a curler, pinging it low and had … forcing Alisson to plunge right to tip around the post.

71 min Kerkez has to go off after taking treatment; he’s off for quite some time and, in the meantime, Calafiori goes down the left, crosses low, and Van Dijk does really well to insert himself in front of Tzolis, poking away from his slide.

68 mins Jacquet slips and Tzolis is in behind down the left! Alisson leaves space at his near post too, and sure’y he’s going to shoot, but instead he squares, seeking Odegaard, only for the recovering Jacquet to slide in and intercept. He has settled brilliantly; as with many things, I think Richie Aprile said it best.

68 min For a team that doesn’t exude joy, I take pleasure i how much sick pleasure Arsenal take in defending. They love the conflict and confrontation, expect themselves to repel attacks, and do anything to back each other up.
67 min It’s time: Ngumoha replaces Gakpo.
66 min Barcola teleports down the left, crosses low, and Wirtz’s touch is poor then, when Madueke carries clear, Kerkez trips him and is booked.

63 min It’s a while since Liverpool created a proper a chance, and the crowd try to get them going. Arsenal have made the game all Bitty McLean these last few minutes, and they can feel the sweat of time expiring.
62 min Change for Arsenal, Lewis-Skelly on for Guimaraes. I think Arteta will want his ability to get the ball up the pitch.

60 min “I don’t buy this line that all of the best attacking players play outside of the Premier League, writes David Wall.” Sure, Lamine Yamal, Kvaratskhelia, and Mbappe are perhaps on another level (I’d argue Dembele is more of a team player than a great individualist). But others are no better than the best in the Premier League, they just look more glamorous in the colours of Real Madrid or Barcelona. For instance, Anthony Gordon has looked brilliant for Barca so far but was average and inconsistent for Newcastle last year. Players like Haarland, Isak, Bruno Fernande (albeit not this year), Saka, Odegaard, and a few others are as individually talented or effective as anyone playing outside the Premier League. They just suffer through familiarity.”

But that’s what I said: the best attackers don’t play in the Prem. You gave a list, and to that we can add Kane, Olise, Bellingham, Raphinha and others. Saka and Odegaard aren’t in that class, while of course Gordon looks better playing in front of Pedri.

58 min Here comes the change, Szoboszlai returning from injury to replace Nyoni. He struggled to control his emotions early on and might’ve been sent off for two bookable offences, but he stabilised thereafter and kept things ticking with hard, simple passes.
57 min I wonder if we might see Ngumoha soon; oh, but on the touchline, Szoboszlai is preparing himself. Presumably, Nyoni will be the man to make way.
56 min Then Nyoni gives Kerkez quick, simple ball, and hew sets off diagonally from the touchline before slipping Isak in behind; from an acute angle, he thrashes over.
55 min Madueke sweeps Barcol’s legs and is booked.

53 min “Winning the league requires winning every week against teams who are almost uniformly top 40, probably top 30 in Europe,” writes Sam Glover. “It’s not glamorous but it’s just as hard as winning four must-wins against good rivals. It’s just a different era.

And how many top players come to the Premier League and crush it, against how many leave the league and crush it elsewhere. The top of the Champions League is just a reflection of the fact that English teams are battered week in, week out and their rivals play their second team in the league.”

I agree with all of this, but I still think the point stands: the standard at the top is not high. Arsenal aren’t close to Guardiola’s City, Klopp’s Liverpool, Mourinho’s Chelsea or Fergie’s two Champions League winners.

51 min We’ve carried on where we left off, Liverpool again peppering the Arsenal box with crosses, again to little avail. Oh but this is better, Nyoni punching into Mac Allister, who turns to Isak, who flicks around the corner for Kerkez … who’s offside. Nevertheless, those are the kind of moves Liverpool need to construct, one-touch passing against which Arsenal’s defence can’t set.
49 min Thinking again about Jasper’s email, the point with Isak isn’t so much about him taking a dive, but making enough of a confident fuss to make sure VAR take a serious look.
48 min Araujo, of whom we’ve seen relatively little, crosses, but the various attackers are on their heels.
items.author: Daniel Harris
items.titleZh: 利物浦 0-1 阿森纳：英超联赛实时战报
items.summaryZh: 哈弗茨进球助阿森纳客场击败利物浦，自2012年以来首次在安菲尔德取胜并登顶积分榜。
bodyZh: 啊哈，大卫·海特纳的比赛报告来了。
这意味着我们的直播到此结束，感谢大家的陪伴和评论——很抱歉没能用到所有的留言——大家再见。
范戴克对天空体育表示，利物浦在最后15分钟本可以做得更多，但他感到失望。他认为他们在失球后踢得更好，麦卡利斯特的头球本可以改变比赛，而且他认为那是一个对伊萨克的明显点球。
当被问及伊萨克是否应该更多地抱怨时，他说有很多摄像机，所以阿森纳做得很好。
他说，当新面孔加入时，需要时间、工作、经历困难时刻等等。球迷们可以看到最近几周已经有了很大的进步，他们拼尽全力，这是最起码的要求，尤其是在利物浦，他们需要的是结果。
VAR对马杜埃凯轻触麦卡利斯特的裁决是“不具攻击性或暴力”。我认为这是一个正确的判罚，但再次说明，我们需要对规则做点什么；目前，我们似乎建立了一种制度，即对无球状态下的轻微犯规和一般急躁情绪的判罚，比可能导致受伤的铲球还要严厉。
我猜Wirtz被签下是为了扮演这个角色，但他看起来无法以足够快的速度来弥补他力量和爆发力的不足。
另一方面，有一些年轻球员正在崭露头角，可能会改变这种状况——马克斯·多曼和里奥·恩古莫哈最为引人注目。
顺便说一句，那场比赛正是为什么我说英超缺乏进攻质量的原因。看着历史上两支身价最高球队的较量，我们在智慧、配合和个人即兴发挥方面几乎看不到什么。速度、强度和身体对抗确实很强，但双方都没有一个能把这一切串联起来的球员。
同时进行的还有：
德克兰·赖斯表示，安菲尔德会制造出一波又一波持续的进攻，但他们开局良好，他们的团结是“无敌的……就像我以前从未见过的那样”。
哈弗茨说利物浦拥有顶级球员并能展现他们的实力，但他们团结一致，共同防守，经历了一些艰难时刻。关于进球，他说90%归功于赖斯——“我们都知道他的右脚”。
回到赖斯，他说主教练在赛季初与他进行了“一次非常坦诚的对话”，告诉他可以做得更多，而在赛前，他告诉哈弗茨要冲击禁区。这是他在安菲尔德的首场胜利，但这并不意味着积分榜上的最终结果；你需要在2月和3月认真对待。在此之前，你只需尽可能赢得更多的比赛。
赖斯被评为全场最佳球员，尽管我会把这个荣誉给加布里埃尔，但我对此没有异议。
亚当·达克说：“他们只是功亏一篑，”但事实是利物浦并没有真正接近。Opta刚刚裁定巴尔科拉的射门不被算作一次射门，所以他们在主场有96分钟的时间没有完成一脚射门；他们有麦卡利斯特击中横梁上方的头球和维尔茨击中横梁的任意球，但几乎没有其他威胁。
或者换句话说，伊劳拉还有工作要做——但他们不会每周都遇到像阿森纳这样防守的球队。
阿森纳自2012年9月以来首次在安菲尔德取胜；米克尔·阿尔特塔在其执教生涯中首次在阿森纳客胜利物浦。凭借集体组织和防守的巨大努力，他们升至积分榜首；要阻止他们卫冕冠军，需要付出巨大的努力。
第90+6分钟，索博斯洛伊向前推进，齐米卡斯的传中尝试被马杜埃凯封堵，当球被重新吊入阿森纳禁区时，拉亚迅速将球没收。
第90+5分钟，阿利松大脚开到前场，范戴克争到第一落点，伊萨克因对加布里埃尔犯规被判犯规。比赛大概就这样了。
第90+4分钟，还剩两分钟，如果不再丢球，阿森纳将稳居榜首。这是一次极其顽强的后防表现，尽管他们并没有面对太多有质量的进攻。
第90+2分钟，巴尔科拉轻射被拉亚轻松化解；这是他们的第一脚射正。拉亚随后因拖延时间被黄牌警告。
第90+1分钟，角球被解围，利物浦卷土重来，但他们的办法在一段时间前就已经用尽了；如果他们除了把球吊入禁区之外真的有什么战术的话。在此之前他们的表现还算体面，但我不太明白他们为什么偏要按照阿森纳希望的方式组织进攻。
第90分钟，又一个球被吊入禁区，范戴克头球摆渡，穆尼奥斯试图在卡拉菲奥里和因卡皮耶之间钻过去抢点，但头球力量不足。不过利物浦延续了进攻，恩古莫哈的传中被封堵出底线获得角球；我们将有六分钟的补时。
第89分钟，阿尔特塔换上梅里诺换下厄德高，这让我想起了上赛季对阵拜仁的比赛，阿森纳通过换上身体强壮的球员来确保胜利。正如温格所说，他们可能缺乏一点细腻，但和他们比赛对任何人来说都不是件趣事。
第88分钟，我以为约克雷斯会早点上场去冲击防线，当索博斯洛伊撞倒厄德高时，刘易斯-斯凯利有机会对付他……但传球力量过大。
第86分钟，利物浦下半场的表现令人失望。禁区周边的配合不够好，而且他们尝试的次数也不够多。但恩古莫哈来了，他带球冲向卡拉菲奥里并晃动了几下，射门被封堵出边线；范戴克现在在踢中锋，所以预计会有更多的传中。
第84分钟，阿森纳做出换人调整，因卡皮耶和约克雷斯换下特佐利斯和哈弗茨。哈弗茨并不是每个人心目中的中锋人选，包括我在内，但他在重大比赛中的纪录是极好的。
第82分钟，利物浦进行人员调整，将踢右后卫的穆尼奥斯、库马斯和齐米卡斯换上，阿劳霍、维尔茨和克尔凯兹下场。
第81分钟，VAR维持原判；很好。麦卡利斯特和廷贝尔双双吃到黄牌；前者为自己的假摔表现感到羞耻。
第79分钟，麦卡利斯特对厄德高犯规，然后弯下腰贴到他脸上，并进行轻微的掌掴以激化矛盾。随后双方自然发生了口角，廷贝尔冲在前面，接着马杜埃凯将额头贴向麦卡利斯特；我不确定是否有前冲动作，但确实有轻微接触，麦卡利斯特像泄了气一样倒地，VAR需要做出裁决。
第77分钟，但与此同时，恩古莫哈用他的弱势脚内切，传中到后点，当范戴克将球顶回时，阿劳霍试图强行射门，但被直接封堵。利物浦仍然没有一脚射正，这充分说明了阿森纳的防守——以及他们在关键时刻缺乏流畅度。
第75分钟，恩古莫哈在右路创造出了空间，但找不到足够大的空当钻过去。我想不久后伊劳拉可能会让他与巴尔科拉对换位置，后者拥有从外线突破的速度，这样他就可以斜向冲击禁区。
第74分钟，我的意思是，刘易斯-斯凯利几分钟前因为撞倒伊萨克被黄牌警告。
第73分钟，阿森纳开始掌控局势，就在我打字的时候，马杜埃凯沿左路推进，横敲给另一侧的特佐利斯。他拉开角度起脚兜射，打出一记低平球……迫使阿利松倒地扑救将球挡出立柱。
第71分钟，克尔凯兹接受治疗后必须离场；他在场外呆了很长时间，与此同时，卡拉菲奥里从左路下底传出低平球，范戴克表现非常出色，抢在特佐利斯之前将球从他的滑铲中捅开。
第68分钟，雅凯滑倒，特佐利斯从左路获得单刀！阿利松在前门柱也留出了空间，他本该射门，但他却选择了横敲寻找厄德高，结果回追的雅凯滑铲将球拦截。他的表现极为出色；正如里奇·阿普里尔（Richie Aprile）所说的那样精辟。
第68分钟，对于一支不怎么流露喜悦的球队来说，我为阿森纳从防守中获得病态的快感而感到高兴。他们热爱冲突和对抗，期望自己能击退进攻，并不惜一切代价互相补位。
第67分钟，是时候了：恩古莫哈换下加克波。
第66分钟，巴尔科拉在左路如闪电般突破并送出低平球传中，维尔茨停球糟糕，随后当马杜埃凯带球突破时，克尔凯兹将其绊倒并吃到黄牌。
第63分钟，利物浦已经有一段时间没有创造出真正的机会了，现场球迷试图为主队加油助威。在过去的几分钟里，阿森纳把比赛变得支离破碎，利物浦能感受到时间流逝带来的煎熬。
第62分钟，阿森纳换人，刘易斯-斯凯利换下吉马良斯。我想阿尔特塔是需要他把球运过半场的能力。

第60分钟，“我不买账那种‘所有最佳进攻球员都在英超之外踢球’的说法，”大卫·沃尔写道。“当然，亚马尔、克瓦拉茨赫利亚和姆巴佩或许处于另一个水平（我认为登贝莱更像是一个团队球员，而不是伟大的个人主义者）。但其他球员并不比英超的顶尖球员差，他们只是身披皇马或巴萨球衣显得更有光彩。例如，安东尼·戈登在巴萨表现出色，但去年在纽卡斯尔却表现平平且不够稳定。像哈兰德、伊萨克、布鲁诺·费尔南德斯（尽管今年不是）、萨卡、厄德高以及其他一些球员，其个人才华或效率并不逊色于任何在英超之外踢球的人。他们只是受到了熟悉程度的影响。”
但这就是我所说的：最好的攻击手不在英超踢球。你列出了一份名单，对此我们还可以加上凯恩、奥利塞、贝林厄姆、拉菲尼亚等人。萨卡和厄德高不在那个级别，当然戈登在佩德里身边踢球看起来更好。
第58分钟，换人调整来了，索博斯洛伊伤愈复出替换恩约尼。他在比赛刚开始时情绪有些失控，本来可能因两次黄牌犯规被罚下，但此后他稳住了阵脚，通过简单硬朗的传球保持了节奏。
第57分钟，我想我们很快就能看到恩古莫哈登场了；哦，但在场边，索博斯洛伊正在做准备。据推测，恩约尼将是离场的人。
第56分钟，随后恩约尼给克尔凯兹送出一脚快速简单的传球，他从边线开始斜向带球突破，然后将球塞到伊萨克身后；从极小的角度，他将球抽高。
第55分钟，马杜埃凯绊倒巴尔科拉被黄牌警告。
第53分钟，“赢得联赛冠军需要在每个星期都战胜那些几乎全是欧洲前40、甚至可能是前30的球队，”萨姆·格洛弗写道。“这并不迷人，但它和在四场必须取胜的比赛中击败强敌一样艰难。这只是不同的时代。”
有多少顶级球员来到英超并大杀四方，又有多少人离开英超并在其他地方大杀四方。欧冠的巅峰只是英格兰球队每周饱受摧残、而他们的竞争对手在联赛中派上替补阵容的写照。
我同意所有这些观点，但我仍然认为重点没有变：顶尖水平并不算高。阿森纳远不及瓜迪奥拉的曼城、克洛普的利物浦、穆里尼奥的切尔西或弗格森的两支欧冠冠军球队。
第51分钟，我们回到了之前的节奏，利物浦再次用传中轰炸阿森纳禁区，但收效甚微。哦，不过这次好多了，恩约尼将球传给麦卡利斯特，后者转身传给伊萨克，伊萨克脚后跟磕给克尔凯兹……但他越位了。尽管如此，这正是利物浦需要建立的进攻套路，通过一脚传球来破解阿森纳无法落位的防守。
第49分钟，再次想到贾斯帕的邮件，关于伊萨克的关键不在于他是否假摔，而在于他要大惊小怪到足以让VAR认真审查的程度。
第48分钟，我们见之不多的阿劳霍送出传中，但多名攻击手反应不及。

bodyEn: It was a game when Arsenal showed their ruthless side and all of the champion knowhow that they ­accumulated over the course of last season. They headed back to London ­having made a statement. Irrespective of what ­happens to ­Manchester City over their financial rule breaches, Arsenal remain the Premier League’s team to beat.

Mikel Arteta was in the Arsenal midfield when the club ­last won a league fixture at Anfield; it was in September 2012, although his memories are a little hazy given the concussion that he sustained in a collision with Jordan Henderson.

Arteta has a clear-eyed focus on retaining the title and this was an occasion for his hopes to surge. Kai Havertz’s first goal in 10 appearances proved the difference but the victory was rooted in Arsenal’s capacity to control and frustrate.

It was a tough watch for the Liverpool crowd and they bayed ­throughout at what they perceived as Arsenal’s use of the dark arts. Arteta’s team won 18 free-kicks and there were some soft ones – each was the prompt for an eruption from the Kop. It said plenty that Virgil van Dijk responded to the full-time whistle by sarcastically applauding the ­referee, Andy Madley. The Liverpool ­captain was booked.

The home team had their grie­vances. Alexander Isak felt Jurriën Timber grab a handful of his shirt in the 21st minute as he tried to reach a Bradley Barcola cross in front of goal. It was a mystery as to why the video assistant referee did not alert Madley. Van Dijk could also be heard shouting in the tunnel afterwards at Noni Madueke, saying the Arsenal winger should have had a second yellow card.

Madueke, who was booked for a foul on Barcola, took a risk when he initiated a touch of foreheads with Alexis Mac Allister towards the end after a melee had broken out. It was sparked by Mac Allister’s ­furious ­reaction to Martin Ødegaard’s ­winning of a free-kick. Liverpool, however, lost any claim to the moral high ground when Mac Allister ­crumpled to the turf in an attempt to get Madueke sent off. The Arsenal player survived. It would have been a harsh dismissal.

In the final analysis, Liverpool did not do enough. They provided high‑energy enjoyment in the first half but they fizzled out, the invention drying up. They ­finished with no shots on target as their five-match winning run in all competitions ground to a halt. Goals remain a problem for them in the league and the truth was ­Arsenal kept them out with a measure of comfort. Arsenal’s previous trip to the north‑west had ended in ­Carabao Cup humiliation at Fleetwood on Tuesday night. This was much more like it.

Liverpool brought the intensity at the outset with Trey Nyoni snapping into challenges on his full league debut. The 19-year-old’s first action was to leave something on Ødegaard and, not long after that, he did the same to Havertz. Nyoni was fortunate to emerge without a yellow card.

The tone was set early, the Kop teeming with indignation at what they saw as Arsenal’s readiness to go down easily and stay down. The match was shaped by Havertz’s goal on 16 minutes and from a Liverpool point of view, it was a self-inflicted wound. Alisson tried to be too cute with a short pass out from his area for Jérémy Jacquet; the weight and direction of it was wrong. But when ­Ødegaard pounced, a stunning piece of interplay followed. Arsenal worked it over and up the right for Declan Rice to flash over the final ball, low and across the corridor of a six-yard-box of uncertainty. Havertz, a player who needed an easy tap-in, got one.

Liverpool responded with more fire and they could have scored before the interval, Mac Allister ­blowing the big chance – a free header from Milos Kerkez’s cross in the 43rd minute. Moments earlier, Florian Wirtz had whipped a free-kick from the left‑hand side against the crossbar.

Arsenal flickered on the break. There were a few times in the first half when they flooded men forward and there were possibilities. This was a long way from being a smash‑and‑grab. Havertz narrowly failed to get a touch to a Bruno ­­Guimarães cross-cum-shot while Timber could not react in front of goal after Madueke volleyed a Christos Tzolis cross back from an acute angle.

Arsenal had the game where they wanted it. They backed themselves to keep Liverpool at bay. It was about their game management. They have become masters at drawing the sting and the longer the second half went on the more assured Arsenal looked. They stifled Liverpool and there remained the sense they could land something on the counter.

When Jacquet slipped in the 68th minute, Arsenal went left to Tzolis and he almost teed up ­Ødegaard. With Alisson out of position, ­Jacquet got back to make an important intervention. Tzolis also forced an excellent save with a first‑time shot for the far corner. ­Liverpool fought a losing battle to keep a lid on their emotions. They huffed and they puffed. The equaliser never looked like coming.

items.titleZh: 哈弗茨闪击破门，阿森纳客场战胜利物浦终结2012年以来联赛安菲尔德不胜
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳客场战胜利物浦，终结了自2012年以来在安菲尔德的联赛不胜纪录。
bodyZh: 这场比赛展现了阿森纳冷酷的一面，以及他们在上赛季积累的冠军经验。带着一份宣言，他们启程返回伦敦。无论曼城因违反财务规则面临什么结果，阿森纳依然是英超最难被击败的球队。
阿尔特塔上一次作为阿森纳球员在安菲尔德赢得联赛客场胜利还要追溯到2012年9月，不过由于当时他在与乔丹·亨德森的碰撞中脑震荡，他的记忆已经有些模糊。
阿尔特塔将全部精力集中在卫冕上，这次客场之旅让他的期望大增。哈弗茨在连续10场比赛后终于打入一球，成为了比赛的关键，但这场胜利的根本在于阿森纳掌控并化解对手攻势的能力。
对于利物浦球迷来说，这是一场艰难的比赛，他们整场比赛都在抗议他们认为阿森纳在使用的“黑暗艺术”。阿尔特塔的球队赢得了18次任意球，其中有一些比较勉强，每一次都引得科普看台一片哗然。范戴克在终场哨响时对主裁判安迪·马德利进行讽刺性的鼓掌，这说明了很多问题。这位利物浦队长被黄牌警告。
主队有他们的怨言。亚历山大·伊萨克认为在第21分钟时，朱廷·廷贝尔在门前争抢布拉德利·巴尔科拉的传中时拉拽了他的球衣。视频助理裁判为何没有提醒马德利令人费解。随后还能听到范戴克在通道里向马杜埃凯大喊，称这位阿森纳边锋本应该吃到第二张黄牌。
马杜埃凯因对巴尔科拉犯规吃到黄牌，在起冲突后与亚历Alexis Mac Allister发生额头对顶时冒了险。冲突是由麦卡利斯特对厄德高赢得任意球的愤怒反应引发的。然而，当麦卡利斯特试图通过倒地来让马杜埃凯被罚下时，利物浦失去了道德制高点。这位阿森纳球员留在了场上。那本可能是一张严厉的红牌。
最终分析表明，利物浦做得还不够。他们在上半场展现了极高的活力，但随后逐渐偃旗息鼓，创造力枯竭。随着他们各项赛事五连胜被终结，他们全场没有一次射正。进球对他们来说依然是个问题，事实是阿森纳相当轻松地将他们挡在了门外。上周二晚上，阿森纳在西北部的上一场比赛还在卡拉宝杯中耻辱地输给弗利特伍德。这场比赛的表现则要好得多。
利物浦开场就展现了高强度，小将特雷·尼奥尼在自己的联赛首秀中积极拼抢。这位19岁球员的第一次动作就是给厄德高留下了一脚，不久之后他对哈弗茨也如法炮制。尼奥尼很幸运没有吃到黄牌。
比赛的基调很早就定下了，科普看台对阿森纳轻易倒地并长时间倒地的做法充满愤怒。比赛在第16分钟由哈弗茨的进球定型，从利物浦的角度来看，这是一个自摆乌龙。阿利森试图在禁区内短传给热雷米·雅凯时过于花哨，传球的力量和方向都不对。但当厄德高抢断后，随后展开了一次精彩的配合。阿森纳将球运作到右侧，德克兰·赖斯送出低平传中，皮球划过充满变数的六码区。哈弗茨需要一个轻松的门前推射，而他也确实得到了。
利物浦随后做出了更有力的回应，并在中场休息前本有机会进球，麦卡利斯特在第43分钟错失良机——接米洛斯·科克茨的传中头球顶高。此前不久，弗洛里安·维尔茨主罚的左侧任意球击中了横梁。

新闻推广之后
阿森纳在反击中偶有闪光。上半场有几次他们大举压上并创造了机会。这绝非一场侥幸偷来的胜利。哈弗茨险些触到布鲁诺·吉马良斯的传射，而马杜埃凯从极小角度将克里斯托斯·特佐利斯的传中凌空垫回门前时，廷贝尔也没能在门前做出反应。
阿森纳掌控了他们想要的比赛节奏。他们坚信自己能够将利物浦拒之门外。关键在于他们的比赛管理。他们已经成为消磨对手斗志的大师，下半场时间越长，阿森纳看起来就越自信。他们压制了利物浦，并且始终让人觉得他们能在反击中给对手致命一击。
当雅凯在第68分钟滑倒时，阿森纳将球打到左路寻找特佐利斯，他差点助攻厄德高。在阿利森失位的情况下，雅凯回防做出了一次关键解围。特佐利斯的一脚远角劲射也迫使对方做出了一次精彩扑救。利物浦为控制情绪进行了一场注定失败的战斗。他们狂呼乱叫。扳平比分的进球从未出现。

items.summaryEn: The story of our determined victory at Anfield
bodyEn: We recorded our first win at Anfield for 14 years thanks to Kai Havertz’s first-half goal.
The German stole in at the far post to convert Declan Rice’s low cross, and it was the only goal of the game, as we dug in to repel everything the hosts had to throw at us after that.
The first half saw plenty of goalmouth action, but Havertz was the only one to find the net.
The rest of the half was mainly about repelling the threat of Liverpool, though we also came close to extending our lead through Bruno and Noni Madueke.

We continued to work hard in the second half, preventing Liverpool from having a single shot on target, to see out a fantastic win at Anfield - our first since 2012 - and go back to the top of the league.
HAVERTZ ON TARGET

The game began at a blistering pace, with Liverpool pressing us high whenever we were in possession. The returning Christos Tzolis, playing his first game for a month, threatened to get in behind the Liverpool back line on the counter attack twice in the opening ten minutes though. The first time his low cross was cut out and the second he ran out of ground before he could send the ball into the box.
Rice then shot well over from 25 yards before we went ahead.

Alisson’s rushed clearance was cut out by Martin Odegaard and the ball was quickly recycled to the advancing Rice on the right. His low cross was perfectly placed, through the corridor of uncertainty, and gleefully tapped home at the far post by Havertz.
The goal made him the all-time leading German goalscorer in Premier League history.
STRONG UNDER PRESSURE

Liverpool responded well to falling behind and started to put us under pressure. Alexander Isak had a glorious chance in front of goal but couldn’t get his head to an inswinging cross before Bruno came to the rescue to stop a Barcola run at the near post.
At the other end Bruno dragged a shot just wide after Tzolis led another counter attack, before Madueke was denied by Alisson at the far post from a deep Tzolis cross.
Liverpool were the more dangerous team though, and we had to stand form as they had their tails up and won a succession of corners.
Virgil van Dijk came close when his header was dangerous, but David Raya got enough on it low down to turn it away.
Florian Wirtz was next to go close. His free kick from a narrow angle beat everyone, and looked to be looping in, but thumped off the cross bar and away.
The crosses continued to rain in. Alexis Mac Allister arrived in front of goal to meet a left wing ball, but planted his header over the bar.

Liverpool were enjoying much more of the possession, and much of the game was being played in and around our own penalty box, but Konsa and Gabriel stood firm as we got to half-time with a narrow lead.
TZOLIS COMES CLOSE
Liverpool came out strongly at the start of the second half too, and we had to remain compact and organised.
We retained a threat on the break, and Tzolis capitalised on a slip to burst into the box, and his cross was heading for Odegaard before a well-timed intervention.
Riccardo Calafiori then saw his low cross cleared on the line as we began to come back into the game again.
Tzolis then forced an excellent lo diving save from Alisson when his first time right-footed shot seemed destined for the bottom corner.
But make no mistake, we were also having to work hard at the back. Jurrien Timber was the next to make a crucial block in his own box.
All the work paid off, as we saw out the win to return to the top of the table – our 300th Premier League away victory.
WHAT’S NEXT

We head back into Europe in midweek, to play Slavia Prague away on Wednesday evening on Matchday Four in the Champions League. Our next Premier League game is at home to Hull City next Saturday before the November international break.

items.titleZh: 战报：利物浦 0-1 阿森纳
items.summaryZh: 凭借哈弗茨在上半场的进球，我们在客场顽强击败利物浦，重返英超积分榜首。
bodyZh: 凭借凯·哈弗茨在上半场的进球，我们自14年来首次在安菲尔德球场取胜。
这位德国球员在远门柱插上，转化了德克兰·赖斯的低平传中，这也是本场比赛的唯一进球，随后我们顶住了主队随后的所有反扑。
上半场创造了许多门前机会，但只有哈弗茨破门得分。
半场剩余时间主要在抵御利物浦的威胁，尽管我们也通过布鲁诺和诺尼·马杜埃凯险些扩大领先优势。
我们在下半场继续努力防守，没有让利物浦获得哪怕一次射正，最终在安菲尔德取得了一场梦幻般的胜利——这是我们自2012年以来的首次——并重回联赛榜首。
哈弗茨建功
比赛以极快的节奏开始，每当我们控球时，利物浦就会进行高位逼抢。复出的克里斯托斯·齐奥利斯在一个月来的首场比赛中，在开局前十分钟内两次险些通过反击突破利物浦防线。第一次他的低平球传中被截断，第二次他在将球送入禁区前球出了底线。
随后赖斯在25码外远射高出，不久后我们便取得了领先。
阿利森仓促的解围被马丁·厄德高截获，皮球迅速传给插上的右路赖斯。他的低平球传中恰到好处，穿过了危险地带，哈弗茨在远门柱轻松推射破门。
这个进球使他成为了英超历史上面进球最多的德国球员。
顶住压力
利物浦在落后后做出积极回应，开始给我们施加压力。亚历山大·伊萨克在门前获得绝佳机会，但未能触及传中，随后布鲁诺在近门柱化解了巴尔科拉的突破。
另一端，在齐奥利斯策动又一次反击后，布鲁诺的射门稍稍偏出，随后马杜埃凯在远门柱接齐奥利斯的传中被阿利森化解。
不过利物浦是更危险的一方，随着他们士气大振并连续赢得角球，我们不得不稳固防守。
维吉尔·范戴克险些破门，他的头球极具威胁，但大卫·拉亚低身化解了险情。
接下来是弗洛里安·维尔茨险些破门。他在狭窄角度的任意球越过了所有人，眼看就要旋入网窝，但击中横梁弹出。
传中雨点般持续袭来。亚历西斯·麦卡利斯特在门前接左路传球，但他的头球顶高了。
利物浦占据了更多控球权，大部分比赛都在我们的禁区内及周边进行，但孔萨和加布里埃尔坚守阵地，让我们带着微弱领先优势进入中场休息。
齐奥利斯险些破门
下半场开始后利物浦同样攻势猛烈，我们必须保持紧凑和有组织。
我们在反击中依然保持威胁，齐奥利斯利用对方滑倒杀入禁区，他的传中眼看要找到厄德高，但对方及时拦截。
随后里卡多·卡拉菲奥里的低平传中在门线上被解围，我们的进攻也开始有所起色。
齐奥利斯随后逼迫阿利森作出了一次精彩的低扑救，他右脚的第一时间射门本已奔向死角。
但毫无疑问，我们的后防线也承受了巨大的工作量。尤里恩·廷贝尔随后在自家禁区内做出了一次关键封堵。
所有的努力都得到了回报，我们守住胜局重回积分榜首——这也是我们在英超的第300场客场胜利。
接下来
我们将于周中重返欧洲赛场，于周三晚上在欧冠第四轮客场对阵布拉格斯拉维亚。我们的下一场英超比赛将于下周六在主场迎战赫尔城，随后迎来11月的国际比赛日。

items.titleEn: Team news: Tzolis returns to action at Anfield
items.summaryEn: Rice, Madueke and Calafiori also start against Liverpool
bodyEn: Winger Christos Tzolis is straight back into the starting line up to face Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League on Sunday.
Our summer signing had missed the last six games after suffering a hamstring injury while on international duty at the start of last month.

Unsurprisingly manager Mikel Arteta makes a host of changes to the side that played in the Carabao Cup in midweek. Indeed of the XI who started at Fleetwood, only Jurrien Timber and Kai Havertz retain their places.

Riccardo Calafiori and Bruno Guimaraes are both recalled to the starting line up after neither were named from the start in our last Premier League game, against Everton last weekend. Noni Madueke is also back to complete the front three with Tzolis and Havertz.
The hosts also make several changes after their midweek cup game – which they won on penalties against Chelsea at Anfield.
Goalkeeper Alisson returns, as do Jeremy Jacquet, Milos Kerkez, Florian Wirtz, Alexis Mac Allister, Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak. Dominik Szoboszlai is fit enough to return to the bench.
Arsenal: Raya, Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori, Rice, Bruno, Odegaard, Madueke, Tzolis, Havertz.Subs: Arrizabalaga, Mosquera, White, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Merino, Zubimendi, Lewis-Skelly.
Liverpool: Alisson, Araujo, Jacquet, van Dijk, Kerkez, Mac Allister, Nyoni, Wirtz, Gakpo, Barcola, Isak.Subs: Mamardashvilli, Gomez, Endo, Szoboszlai, Tsimikas, Munoz, Gravenberch, Koumas, Ngumoha.

items.titleZh: 球队新闻：齐奥利斯在安菲尔德复出
items.summaryZh: 赖斯、马杜埃凯和卡拉菲奥里也将对阵利物浦首发出场。
bodyZh: 边锋赫里斯托斯·齐奥利斯直接重回首发阵容，将随阿森纳在周日的英超联赛中客场挑战安菲尔德的利物浦。
我们的这位夏窗新援在上个月初的国家队比赛日遭遇腿筋受伤后，已经连续缺席了过去六场比赛。
毫无疑问，主教练米克尔·阿尔特塔对周中参加联赛杯的阵容进行了大幅轮换。在弗利特伍德首发的十一人中，只有于尔里安·廷贝尔和卡伊·哈弗茨保留了主力位置。
里卡尔多·卡拉菲奥里和布鲁诺·吉马良斯双双重回首发阵容，此前他们二人均未在上周末对阵埃弗顿的英超联赛中首发。诺尼·马杜埃凯也回归首发，与齐奥利斯和哈弗茨组成进攻三叉戟。
主队在经历周中的杯赛后也进行了多次人员调整，他们在安菲尔德通过点球大战击败了切尔西。
门将阿利森回归，杰里米·雅凯、米洛斯·克尔凯兹、弗洛里安·维尔茨、亚历克西斯·麦卡利斯特、布拉德利·巴尔科拉和亚历山大·伊萨克也悉数回归。多米尼克·索博斯洛伊身体状况良好，重回替补席。
阿森纳：拉亚、廷贝尔、孔萨、加布里埃尔、卡拉菲奥里、赖斯、布鲁诺、厄德高、马杜埃凯、齐奥利斯、哈弗茨。替补：阿里萨巴拉加、莫斯克拉、怀特、因卡皮耶、埃泽、哲凯赖什、梅里诺、祖比门迪、刘易斯-斯凯利。
利物浦：阿利森、阿劳霍、雅凯、范戴克、克尔凯兹、麦卡利斯特、尼奥尼、维尔茨、加克波、巴尔科拉、伊萨克。替补：马马尔达什维利、戈麦斯、远藤航、索博斯洛伊、齐米卡斯、穆尼奥斯、赫拉芬贝赫、库马斯、恩古莫哈。

items.titleEn: Alessia: “We should have been more ruthless”
items.summaryEn: Alessia Russo felt a point was the least we deserved in Sunday’s 1-1 draw at home to Aston Villa in the Women’s Super League.
bodyEn: Alessia Russo felt a point was the least we deserved in Sunday’s 1-1 draw at home to Aston Villa in the Women’s Super League.

The visitors opened the scoring against the run of play in the 25th minute by way of Chasity Grant, but we eventually got our equaliser with five minutes left on the clock when Russo headed in from a Stina Blackstenius delivery.

Reflecting on the result, Russo said: “I think we should have been more ruthless throughout the game that we could have won here today. We've been on a good run and we want to continue that. But yes, this league's tough. Home and away, you've got to be at 100% and we were there in moments, but not for all of the game today.”

Asked how the players pick themselves up when we’re creating so many chances, only to concede the opener, Alessia continued: “It’s difficult. The goal doesn't help. But yes, like I said, these teams, even teams that you don't consider to be the top four, they have so much quality.
“Aston Villa are a really hard team, but we've got to be better. We had spells, we had moments, we created. But yes, we've got to put the ball in the back of the net.”
The energy inside Emirates Stadium was tangible was Russo had buried the equaliser, with supporters off their seats and urging us on to a late winner.
“It felt great,” Russo said. “It definitely spurred us on. I think, yes, it's a shame there was so little time left. But no, they're great. They show up every week and yes, we needed them.”

Some supporters will be getting up in the early hours of next Sunday to make the long trip up to Mersyside for our 12pm kick-off against Liverpool at Anfield, so Russo is keen to get back to winning ways for our Gooners.

“That fixture's early and we know the dedication that they put in,” she added. “So yes, it's about us now. We need to perform for them, for ourselves, for everyone around Arsenal. And yes, we've had some good moments this season and some challenging ones, but now it's about how we react.”

items.titleZh: 阿莱西亚：我们本该更加杀伐果断
items.summaryZh: 阿莱西亚·鲁索认为在周日主场对阵阿斯顿维拉的比赛中，收获一分是至少应得的。
bodyZh: 在周日英超女足联赛主场1-1战平阿斯顿维拉的比赛后，阿莱西亚·鲁索认为收获一分是球队至少应得的结果。
客队在第25分钟趁势由查西蒂·格兰特打破僵局，但在比赛还剩五分钟时，鲁索接斯蒂娜·布拉克斯特纽斯的传中头球破门，最终帮助我们扳平了比分。
在回顾这场比赛结果时，鲁索表示：“我认为我们在整场比赛中本该更加果断，今天我们本可以赢下比赛。我们之前状态不错，并且希望延续下去。但事实是，这个联赛很艰难。无论主客场，你都必须拿出100%的状态，今天我们在某些时刻做到了，但并非整场比赛都如此。”
当被问及在创造了如此多机会却先失一球的情况下，球员们如何重整旗鼓时，阿莱西亚继续说道：“这很困难。丢球无济于事。但就像我说的，这些球队，甚至是那些你认为不在前四之列的球队，都具备很强的实力。”
“阿斯顿维拉是一支非常难缠的球队，但我们必须做得更好。我们有过阶段性的优势，有过机会，也创造出了威胁。然而，我们必须把球送入球门。”
当鲁索打入扳平进球时，酋长球场内的氛围十分热烈，球迷们离开座位，敦促我们在最后时刻争取绝杀。
鲁索说：“感觉太棒了。这确实激励了我们。遗憾的是留给我们的时间太少了。不过他们太棒了，每周都会到场支持，我们需要他们。”
下周日清晨，一些球迷将早早出发，开启前往默西塞德郡的漫长旅程，观看中午12点在安菲尔德球场对阵利物浦的比赛。因此，鲁索渴望用一场胜利来回馈枪迷。
她补充道：“这场比赛开球时间很早，我们深知球迷们付出的奉献。所以，现在关键在于我们自己。我们需要为球迷、为我们自己、为阿森纳的每一个人拿出好的表现。本赛季我们有过精彩时刻，也有过严峻挑战，而现在关键在于我们如何做出反应。”

items.titleEn: Renée disappointed with our start against Villa
items.summaryEn: Slegers felt the way we started Sunday’s 1-1 draw at home to Aston Villa in the WSL was what let us down in the end
bodyEn: Renée Slegers felt the way we started Sunday’s 1-1 draw at home to Aston Villa in the Women’s Super League was what let us down in the end.
We were dominant in N5 in terms of possession and chance creation, but could only get the one goal late on to show for it when Stina Blackstenius’ cross was headed in by Alessia Russo.

Asked how she reflects on the match, our head coach said: “Very disappointing performance from us. I think even though we create good chances, clear good chances in the second half mostly and towards the end, the start from our side isn't good enough and that's a collective responsibility.

“The ball speed, the speed of the game, the energy on the pitch in the first half, we want to bring more. I think that doesn't set the tone for us in the game and then we end up chasing it in the second half.”
It was a similar setup to what we’ve faced on a number of occasions already in 2026/27, with our opponents sitting back in a low block and looking to break on the counter-attack.
Renée felt we created more than enough opportunities though to overcome that obstacle.

“I think there's chances today to finish it. I think where we were so good against Benfica with the calmness and composure in the box, you could see. I think it has to do with the first half not creating enough and not setting the intensity and the tone for the game, then everything becomes more rushed in the second half and we lose a little bit of composure in the final third.”
We asked Renée if our players can look to punish teams more quickly when we win the ball, and not allow them to get back into their defensive shape before we create a goalscoring opportunity.
“Yeah, definitely,” she agreed. “I think Benfica was a positive example of capitalising on transition moments when there's more space, going forward faster.

“But yes, I think everything has to do with the way we played in the first half. Yes, we play with urgency and we scored that goal in the second half, but we don't set ourselves up well enough from the start.”
Renée added that there was no update on Steph Catley’s fitness, after she had to be withdrawn in the second half.
“I haven't spoken to the medical team yet, so I hope she's okay,” she said.

items.titleZh: 雷妮对阵维拉的开局表现感到失望
items.summaryZh: 雷妮认为周日主场1-1战平阿斯顿维拉的比赛中，球队的开局表现最终让我们付出了代价。
bodyZh: 雷妮·斯莱格斯（Renée Slegers）认为，在周日进行的女子英超联赛中，我们在主场1-1战平阿斯顿维拉的比赛里，球队的开局方式正是最终让我们失望的原因。
我们在主场占据了控球率和创造机会方面的绝对优势，但直到比赛尾声时，才由斯蒂娜·布拉克斯特纽斯传中、阿莱西亚·鲁索头球破门，收获了唯一的一粒进球。
当被问及对这场比赛的看法时，我们的主教练表示：“对我们来说这是一场非常令人失望的表现。我认为尽管我们创造出了不错的机会，尤其是下半场和尾声阶段创造出了绝佳机会，但我们的开局表现还不够好，这是集体责任。”
“上半场的传球速度、比赛节奏以及球场上的能量，都是我们想要提升的。我认为这没有为我们的比赛定下基调，导致我们在下半场只能疲于追赶。”
这种情况与我们在2026/27赛季已经多次面对的局面类似，当时我们的对手选择回收防守摆出低位防线，并寻求通过反击制造威胁。
不过，雷妮认为我们创造了足够多的机会来克服这一障碍。
“我认为今天本有机会杀死比赛。我们可以看到，我们在对阵本菲卡时展现出了禁区内的冷静与沉着。我认为这与上半场创造机会不足、未能为比赛奠定强度和基调有关，这导致下半场一切都变得更加急躁，我们在进攻三区失去了一些冷静。”
我们询问雷妮，当球队赢得球权时，球员们是否可以更快地惩罚对手，而不是在创造得分机会之前让对手重新落好防守位置。
“是的，完全可以，”她表示赞同。“我认为本菲卡是一个积极的例子，在有更多空间时利用转换瞬间更快地向前推进。”
“但是的，我认为这一切都与我们上半场的踢法有关。是的，我们踢出了紧迫感并在下半场取得了进球，但我们从一开始就没有为自己打下足够好的基础。”
雷妮补充说，在斯蒂芬·卡特利（Steph Catley）于下半场被换下后，目前还没有关于她身体状况的最新消息。
她说：“我还没和医疗团队交流过，所以我希望她没事。”

items.summaryEn: We drew 1-1 with Aston Villa in the Women’s Super League at Emirates Stadium on Sunday afternoon.
bodyEn: We drew 1-1 with Aston Villa in the Women’s Super League at Emirates Stadium on Sunday afternoon.
Chasity Grant gave the away side the lead against the run of play in the 25th minute and, despite creating plenty of chances, it seemed as though we'd be unable to find a way back into the game.
Alessia Russo made sure that wasn't the case late on, heading in a Stina Blackstenius cross to equalise.
ALL-OUT ATTACK

We created plenty of chances throughout the first half, starting with Caitlin Foord receiving the ball from Russo in a dangerous area and going for goal with power, but it was straight at Akane Okuma.
Geraldine Reuteler’s cross from the right then reached Foord on the left wing, and she dragged her shot wide of the bottom left.
Moments later, Russo found Georgia Stanway who showed good footwork to create an opening and her strike had too much on it for Okuma, who could only spill it behind for a corner.
Stanway then puts good weight on her pass for the run of Taylor Hinds, whose shot was again pushed past the post.
Hinds spotted Russo down the left wing and she drifts inside before firing wide of the bottom right from distance, and we would soon be punished for not hitting the target.
Grant broke through down the right and saw her shot deflected off of Steph Catley and into the back of the net for 1-0 to Villa.
EAGER TO EQUALISE
In response, Reuteler got a shot away while surrounded by Villa defenders in a tight area, but Okuma was equal to it, and Catley had a corner headed wide by Kyra Cooney-Cross.

Russo teed up Stanway who drove a shot towards goal venomously, but again it was too central to trouble Okuma. A Leah Williamson’s cross came out to Cooney-Cross on brink of half-time and she volleyed wide of the bottom right as we went into the break a goal behind.
SECOND-HALF TWEAKS
Renée Slegers made two changes at half-time, bringing Emily Fox on for her 100th Arsenal appearance alongside Lisa Baum, as they replaced Hinds and Reuteler.

Early in the second half, Ona Batlle picked out Russo and her ball across goal just evaded Foord on the way into Okuma’s gloves, before Russo produced a clever backheel into the path of Fox and her effort was deflected behind for a corner.
Fox then took us forward on the counter-attack and Foord crosses towards the far post, but the ball flew over Baum’s head and out for a goal kick.

Stanway shot into the side netting from a narrow angle on her left foot inside the 18-yard box after being played in by Olivia Smith. Catley returned to the field of play after going off with a knock and forced a block before Baum’s effort was saved by Okuma.
Smith then made way for Kim Little and Elisa de Almeida came on for Catley.

Into the 77th minute, Little’s left-footed toe-poke was goalbound, but Okuma did well to tip it over the bar. We then made another change with seven minutes left on the clock as Blackstenius came on for Cooney-Cross.
We finally found a way through in the 85th minute, as Blackstenius’ cross from the right was headed into the bottom left by Russo for 1-1.

The late winner almost came in the 92nd minute when Stanway played a nice one-two before firing wide of the post, and Foord was next to curl the ball off target before Batlle had a shot saved as the points were ultimately shared.
WHAT'S NEXT
We head to Merseyside next weekend to take on Liverpool at Anfield in Sunday's 12pm kick-off, which tickets are on general sale for.
Then, we're off to Spain to face Barcelona in the UEFA Women's Champions League on Thursday, November 12 (5.45pm kick-off UK time). Again, tickets are on general sale for this fixture at Camp Nou.

items.titleZh: 战报：阿森纳女足 1-1 阿斯顿维拉
items.summaryZh: 周日下午在酋长球场进行的英超女足联赛中，阿森纳1-1战平阿斯顿维拉。
bodyZh: 周日下午在酋长球场进行的英超女足联赛中，我们以1-1战平阿斯顿维拉。
比赛进行到第25分钟时，查西蒂·格兰特在一次反击中攻破球门，帮助客队取得领先。尽管我们创造了大量机会，但似乎很难扳平比分。
比赛尾声阶段，阿莱西亚·鲁 Russo通过头球破门将比分扳平，她接到了斯蒂娜·布拉克斯特纽斯的传中。
全线进攻
我们在上半场创造了许多机会，首先是凯特琳·福德在危险区域接到鲁索的传球后大力射门，但球正中大久保茜的下怀。
随后，杰拉丁·罗伊特勒从右路传中找到左路的福德，她的射门偏出了左下角。
片刻之后，鲁索找到乔治亚·斯坦威，后者通过出色的脚法制造了空间，她的射门力量极大，大久保茜只能将球扑出底线送出角球。
随后，斯坦威为泰勒·海因斯的插上送出精妙传球，但后者的射门再次被扑出底线。
海因斯发现了左路的鲁索，鲁索内切后在远距离起脚射门偏出右下角，我们很快因未能命中目标而受到惩罚。
格兰特从右路突破，她的射门经过斯蒂芬·卡特里的折射飞入球网，维拉1-0领先。
渴望扳平
作为回应，罗伊特勒在维拉后卫的密集防守中完成了一脚射门，但大久保茜稳稳将球抱住，卡特里主罚的角球被基拉·库尼-克罗斯头球顶偏。
鲁索为斯坦威做球，后者大力轰门，但球路太正没能对大久保茜构成威胁。半场结束前，莉亚·威廉姆斯的传球落到库尼-克罗斯脚下，她的凌空抽射偏出了右下角，我们带着一球落后的劣势进入中场休息。
下半场调整
雷妮·斯勒格尔在半场进行了两次换人，埃米莉·福克斯替补登场迎来她的阿森纳各项赛事第100场出场，丽莎·鲍姆也一同替补登场，换下了海因斯和罗伊特勒。
下半场伊始，奥娜·巴特莱找到鲁索，鲁索横传门区但福德在球进入大久保茜手套前差之毫厘。随后鲁索巧妙脚后跟做球给福克斯，后者的射门被折射出底线。
福克斯随后策动反击，福德传中到后点，但球飞过了鲍姆的头顶出了底线。
斯坦威在禁区内接奥利维亚·史密斯的传球后，用左脚从狭窄角度劲射击中边网。卡特里在伤退后重新回到场上并迫使对手完成一次封堵，随后鲍姆的射门被大久保茜扑出。
随后史密斯被金·利特尔换下，埃莉萨·德阿尔梅达替补登场换下卡特里。
比赛进行到第77分钟，利特尔左脚脚尖捅射直奔球门，大久保茜表现出色将球托出横梁。比赛还剩七分钟时我们再次换人，布拉克斯特纽斯换下库尼-克罗斯。
我们在第85分钟终于打破僵局，布拉克斯特纽斯右路传中，鲁索头球攻入球门左下角，比分改写为1-1。
比赛第92分钟我们险些完成绝杀，斯坦威在一脚精彩的二过一配合后射门偏出立柱，随后福德的弧线球也偏出球门，巴特莱的射门也被扑出，最终双方握手言和。
接下来
下周末我们将前往默西赛德郡，在周日中午12点开球的比赛中客场对阵利物浦（安菲尔德球场），目前该场比赛门票正在公开售票中。
随后，我们将前往西班牙，于11月12日星期四（英国时间下午5点45分）在欧洲女足冠军联赛中对阵巴塞罗那。这场在诺坎普球场的比赛门票同样正在公开售票中。

items.summaryEn: There were two hat-tricks and ten goals in a pulsating London derby on Saturday afternoon
bodyEn: Our young Gunners came out on top in one of the games of the U18 Premier League season, coming from behind to beat Brentford 6-4 in an exhilarating contest.
Vincent Joseph gave us an early lead before Jay Nwosu struck twice in quick succession for Brentford to turn the game around.
We hit back quickly though, with Hashi levelling from the penalty spot before Joseph netted twice more to complete a first-half hat-trick.
Nwosu scored from the first shot of the second half to make it 4-3, before Abraham Owusu-Gyasi restored our two goal cushion, only for Nwosu to score his fourth of the afternoon to make it 5-4.
But it was Hashi who had the final say, completing a brace to secure the most exciting of victories at the Sobha Realty Training Centre.
Press play on the video at the top of the article to watch all ten goals from Saturday's contest.

items.summaryZh: 周六下午的一场伦敦德比上演十球大战，双方共完成两次帽子戏法。
bodyZh: 我们的年轻枪手在U18英超联赛的一场精彩较量中笑到最后，他们在落后的情况下以6-4逆转战胜布伦特福德。
文森特·约瑟夫为我们早早取得领先，随后杰伊·努沃苏为布伦特福德连进两球反超比分。
不过我们迅速做出回应，哈希通过点球扳平比分，随后约瑟夫再进两球，在上半场就完成了帽子戏法。
下半场刚开始努沃苏就攻入一球将比分改写为4-3，随后亚伯拉罕·奥苏-贾西为我们重新建立两球优势，但努沃苏打入个人本场第四球将比分追至5-4。
不过最终由哈希锁定胜局，他在索巴地产训练基地上演梅开二度，确保球队取得这场极其精彩的胜利。

items.summaryEn: Renée Slegers has made just one change to the starting line-up for this afternoon’s Women’s Super League clash with Aston Villa
bodyEn: Renée Slegers has made just one change to the starting line-up for this afternoon’s Women’s Super League clash with Aston Villa.
Leah Williamson replaces Elisa de Almeida in defence following Wednesday’s 3-0 win at home to Benfica in the UEFA Women’s Champions League.
Otherwise, it’s as you were, with Misa Rodriguez in goal behind defenders Ona Batlle, Steph Catley and Taylor Hinds.
Kyra Cooney-Cross, Georgia Stanway and Geraldine Reuteler are the midfield three, with Caitlin Foord, Alessia Russo and Olivia Smith on the forward line.

items.summaryZh: 雷妮·斯勒格斯对阵阿斯顿维拉的首发阵容做出了一处调整。

bodyEn: English football loves the word “dossier”. It doesn’t love dossiers themselves, of course; they’re for nerds – unless, that is, they’re a “secret dossier”, which have a thrilling redolence of spy dramas, invisible ink and dead drops. Non-secret dossiers, though, are inherently risible: call something a “dossier” in English football and you’re immediately signalling: this is absurd poindextering. Dossiers were preposterous when Don Revie was – imagine the pretension! – drawing up scouting reports on opposing players, and they are preposterous today as Mikel Arteta collates images of rival managers stepping outside their technical area.

Arteta, it should be said, did not use the word “dossier”; rather it was swiftly applied to what he had called “a massive storage of images”. During Arsenal’s 2-0 win against Everton last Saturday, he received his second booking of the season for leaving his technical area. This, it turns out, is another part of the vast conspiracy against Arsenal. Yes, Arteta accepted, he left his technical area (44 times before being booked, according to the former referee Graham Scott), but other managers do it too. “There are managers who have the record in the league, 36 times in 10 minutes [they] leave the touchline – no yellows,” he said. “I am clipping all of that … so if somebody comes to me I can say: ‘I am not in the record yet.’ Somebody else has the record so let’s see. Then it’s 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the managers.”

There are two ways of looking at this. Perhaps it’s genuine. Perhaps Arteta really is a ludicrous Pooterish figure, counting the misdemeanours of others, the worst kind of neighbourhood watch curtain-twitcher who happens also to have been cursed with a persecution complex: “I got a fine because my parking permit was partially obscured, but Mr Emery at No 17 has been six inches out of his bay on at least three occasions this month and … nothing.” Or perhaps he really is an inveterate snitch, glorying in telling on his peers: “Please, Miss! Miss, Daniel’s been chewing gum again, Miss.”

Or, perhaps awed by the misguided defiance of Manchester City fans after their club was found to have perpetrated the greatest act of cheating in English sporting history, he is trying to persuade his base that everybody is against Arsenal to generate a siege mentality. Declan Rice mystifyingly got away with kicking Malick Yalcouyé off the ball against Brighton, but it’s important to remember that Arsenal remain the real victims here.

The history of mind games in football is long and storied. Before the 1939 FA Cup final, for instance, Major Frank Buckley, the flamboyant manager of Wolves, claimed to have injected his players with “animal secretions”. A French surgeon, Serge Voronoff, had begun transplanting tissue from monkey testicles on to human testicles as an anti-ageing treatment, and it was widely believed that it was this monkey gland treatment that Buckley was employing. In fact, he almost certainly gave his players nothing stronger than vitamins but the idea was that Wolves’ morale would be boosted, while their opponents in the final, Portsmouth, would be intimidated by the prospect of taking on players juiced up on simian fluids. It didn’t work, Portsmouth winning 4-1 despite finishing 15 places below Wolves in the table, but the logic is familiar.

The monkey glands were relatively benign, little more than a publicity stunt, but it’s easy for attempts at psychological manipulation to take on a darker aspect. Before Inter played Liverpool in the second leg of the 1965 European Cup semi-final, for instance, their manager, Helenio Herrera, had 100,000 leaflets distributed claiming that at the end of the first leg at Anfield, Liverpool fans had sung “Go home, Italians” to the tune of “Santa Lucia” which supposedly was intended “to deride us and make us feel we are just a race of cheap mandolin players”. Suitably enraged, Inter fans ensured San Siro seethed with fury, which perhaps encouraged some questionable refereeing decisions (although it probably wasn’t the only factor) as Liverpool lost 3-0 and went out 4-3 on aggregate.

Alex Ferguson was a master of the art, while José Mourinho openly acknowledged that the next game begins in the post-match press conference for the previous one. Mourinho, in particular, often crossed the line of professional decency. Arteta, clearly, is not at that level, at least not yet, but if his dossier is part of a deliberate strategy it is a dangerous one.

Arteta’s conspiracy theory is likely to find fertile ground among certain online Arsenal fans, who remain convinced that referees have been machinating against them for years. Even on Tuesday there were those who leaped to the defence of Max Dowman after he had been sent off for thrusting a knee towards Harrison Neal’s chest, even though Arteta himself appeared furious with the 16-year-old’s petulance. Why, ran the argument, had Cole Palmer not been shown a straight red for retaliating against Mateus Fernandes in Chelsea’s defeat by Tottenham on Saturday? Dowman went with his knee and Palmer with his belly, which is perhaps enough to explain the discrepancy, but even if it isn’t, so what? If you don’t want to be punished, don’t go thrusting knees or bellies or anything at opponents, no matter how bad a foul they’ve just committed.

It’s not only that football is groaning under the weight of the paranoia of various fan groups, each adamant that Pro Ref is acting with the rosicrucians, the Masons, the mob, Opus Dei and the Cubans to deny their club a spot in the Europa League, a distraction that deflects from the game’s true crisis: its descent from an endeavour in which sporting merit and integrity are paramount into a grimly capitalistic vehicle to make very rich and powerful people even richer and more powerful.

It’s also dangerous because a mood of insecurity, of being convinced everything is against you, is not conducive to winning league titles – as Arsenal know. In 2024-25, their title bid was undermined by their early-season ill discipline, each red card greeted not with the resilience of champions but with bleating about how it wasn’t really their fault and everybody was picking on them, including the injury gods.
Abdicating responsibility rarely helps, snitches seldom prosper and, in English football, dossiers are always a bad idea.

items.titleZh: 若米克尔·阿尔特塔的资料集是一项刻意策略，这对阿森纳来说极其危险 | 乔纳森·威尔逊
items.summaryZh: 阿尔特塔收集对手教练越界的画面引发争议，若此阴谋论是刻意策略，对阿森纳而言将十分危险。
bodyZh: 英格兰足球界喜欢用“资料集（dossier）”这个词。当然，人们并不真正喜欢资料集本身，那是书呆子的玩意——除非它是“秘密资料集”，带有一种间谍剧、隐形墨水和死信箱的刺激氛围。然而，非秘密资料集的本质是可笑的：在英格兰足球中，把某样东西称为“资料集”就是在明确释放信号：这是荒谬的学究气。当唐·里维（Don Revie）——想象一下那种假惺惺的做作——为对手球员制作球探报告时，资料集就显得荒谬，而今天米克尔·阿尔特塔（Mikel Arteta）收集对手教练跨出技术区域的影像时，同样荒谬。

需要指出的是，阿尔特塔本人并没有使用“资料集”这个词；这个词很快就被贴在了他所说的“海量影像存储”上。在上周六阿森纳2-0战胜埃弗顿的比赛中，他因离开技术区域而收到了本赛季的第二张黄牌。事实证明，这是针对阿森纳庞大阴谋的又一部分。是的，阿尔特塔承认他离开了技术区域（据前裁判格雷厄姆·斯科特统计，在被黄牌警告前有44次），但其他教练也这么做。“有些教练在联赛中保持着记录，10分钟内36次离开教练指挥区——却没有黄牌，”他说。“我把所有这些都剪辑下来……所以如果有人来找我说事，我可以回答：‘我的纪录还没到呢。’别人保持着纪录，让我们拭目以待。那么接下来就是10分钟内给教练出示36张黄牌。”

看待这件事有两种方式。也许这是真情流露。也许阿尔特塔真的成了一个荒唐可笑的普特（Pooterish）式人物，数着别人的轻罪，就像那种最糟糕的社区守望相助中爱窥视窗帘的小人，偏巧又患有被害妄想症：“我因为停车证部分被遮挡而罚款，但17号的埃米利县先生这个月至少有三次把车停在车位外面六英寸……却什么事都没有。”或者他真的成了一个根深蒂固的小报告分子，以告发同行为乐：“老师！老师，丹尼又在嚼口香糖了，老师。”
或者，也许是被曼城球迷在俱乐部被发现实施了英格兰体育史上最大作弊行为后表现出的那种被误导的挑衅所震撼，他正试图向其基本盘灌输所有人都在与阿森纳作对的想法，从而营造一种围城心态。德克兰·赖斯（Declan Rice）在对阵布莱顿的比赛中无球踢倒马利克·亚尔库耶（Malick Yalcouyé）却离奇地逃脱了惩罚，但重要的是要记住，阿森纳仍然是这里真正的受害者。

足球界心理战的历史悠久且充满传奇。例如，在1939年足总杯决赛之前，狼队张扬的主帅弗兰克·巴克利（Frank Buckley）少校声称给他的球员注射了“动物分泌物”。一位法国外科医生谢尔盖·沃罗诺夫（Serge Voronoff）曾开始将猴子睾丸组织移植到人类睾丸上作为抗衰老疗法，人们普遍认为巴克利采用的就是这种猴腺疗法。事实上，他给球员使用的东西几乎不可能比维生素更强烈，但其目的是为了提升狼队的士气，同时让决赛对手朴茨茅斯因为要对付注入了类人猿体液的球员而感到畏惧。这并没有起作用，朴茨茅斯以4-1获胜，尽管他们在积分榜上比狼队低了15位，但这种逻辑却是大家熟悉的。

猴腺疗法相对温和，不过是个宣传噱头，但心理战的尝试很容易呈现出更黑暗的一面。例如，在国际米兰对阵利物浦的1965年欧洲冠军杯半决赛次回合之前，他们的主帅海伦尼奥·埃雷拉（Helenio Herrera）散发了10万份传单，声称在安菲尔德的首回合比赛结束后，利物浦球迷曾伴着《圣露西亚》的曲调高唱“回你们的意大利去吧”，这据称旨在“嘲笑我们，让我们觉得我们只是一个廉价曼陀林演奏者的民族”。在被彻底激怒后，国际米兰球迷确保了圣西罗球场怒火中烧，这或许促使裁判做出了一些值得商榷的判决（尽管这可能不是唯一的因素），最终利物浦0-3失利，总比分3-4被淘汰。
亚历克斯·弗格森（Alex Ferguson）是这门艺术的大师，而何塞·穆里尼奥（José Mourinho）则公开承认，下一场比赛是从上一场的赛后新闻发布会开始的。尤其是穆里尼奥，经常越过职业体面的底线。显然，阿尔特塔还没有达到那个水平，至少目前还没有，但如果他的资料集是一项刻意策略，那将是一个危险的策略。

阿尔特塔的阴谋论很可能会在某些在线阿森纳球迷中找到肥沃的土壤，他们仍然坚信裁判多年来一直在密谋对付他们。甚至在周二，还有人跳出来为麦克斯·唐曼（Max Dowman）辩护，此前他因用膝盖撞击哈里森·尼尔（Harrison Neal）的胸部而被罚下，尽管阿尔特塔本人似乎对这位16岁球员的暴躁脾气怒不可遏。反驳的论点是，为什么在切尔西周六输给托特纳姆热刺的比赛中，科尔·帕尔默（Cole Palmer）因对马特乌斯·费尔南德斯（Mateus Fernandes）进行报复而没有被直接红牌罚下？唐曼用的是膝盖，帕尔默用的是肚子，这或许足以解释两者的差异，但即使解释不了，那又怎样？如果你不想受到惩罚，就不要把膝盖、肚子或任何东西撞向对手，无论他们刚才犯规有多严重。

不仅是足球在各种球迷群体的偏执重压下呻吟，每个球迷群体都坚信职业裁判在与玫瑰十字会、共济会、黑帮、主业会和古巴人勾结，剥夺他们俱乐部参加欧联杯的资格，这种干扰转移了人们对足球真正危机的视线：它从一项将体育精神和正直放在首位的运动，沦为了一个严酷的资本主义工具，旨在让非常富有和强大的人变得更加富有和强大。
这也之所以危险，是因为一种不安全感、确信一切都对你不利的氛围，并不利于赢得联赛冠军——正如阿森纳所知。在2024-25赛季，他们的争冠努力由于赛季初期的纪律涣散而受到破坏，每一次红牌迎来的不是冠军的韧性，而是关于错不在他们、所有人都在找他们麻烦（包括伤病之神）的抱怨。
推卸责任很少有帮助，打小报告的人很少能飞黄腾达，而在英格兰足球中，资料集永远都是个坏主意。

items.summaryEn: Our academy coach reflects on a crazy game against Brentford
bodyEn: Our under-18s coach Josh Smith was amazed by the high-scoring clash with Brentford, as we came away 6-4 victors to pick up another three points in U18 Premier League South.
Vincent Joseph bagged a hat-trick, while Maalik Hashi struck twice and Axel Donczew also got in on the act as we held off a relentless opposition.
"Wow, what a game. We knew as players and staff that Brentford have now scored 33 goals in nine games, so we knew their threat.

"What's really pleasing today is that, when we spoke about it [missing chances] after Villa, we were disappointed. The amount of entries and chances that we did have, we didn't score enough, but today we've ended up scoring six.
"However, we're happy but not satisfied. There are a lot of goals that shouldn't have happened today. But yeah, overall, pleased."

Joseph, who made his first start for our under-18s side, seized the opportunity with a treble of goals to help beat the Bees and received praise for his efforts. "Really pleased for him", Josh said. "I thought he was a real handful in terms of his hold-up play, his link-up play and his pressing.
"Really pleased with Vinny today. He had a great start."
With no Premier League 2 fixtures over the weekend, the London derby provided valuable game time for several of our regular under-21s players to feature within their age group.

Josh highlighted the ethos that runs throughout our academy sides and the importance of embedding the same mentality across every age group, both on and off the pitch. "We feel as staff that that comes from training.
"We had a group of lads that played in the under-21s on Tuesday and there'll be a group that will play on Wednesday for the under-19s.
"If we can have the consistent messages for when they do come back to the under-18s programme, I think that really helps them.
"I do feel, in terms of the general connections right now with the new players, the first years, the second years, it's been very positive so far this season."
Josh reflected on the importance of maintaining high standards and developing a tenacious attitude throughout the academy, matching that of our men's team.
He also echoed the need for players to take responsibility for driving those standards themselves, as the group continues to make progress.
"I've said it for the last few weeks, just in terms of finding that consistency, having that relentlessness to keep pushing.
"Then we want a group of lads that are self-regulating, that they can drive the standards themselves and that's what we've been pushing for.
"We feel like they're starting to turn a corner now. So it's about keeping the standards high for them and just their consistent behaviours."

items.summaryZh: 阿森纳U18教练回顾了一场对阵布伦特福德的疯狂进球大战。
bodyZh: 我们的U18主教练乔什·史密斯对这场与布伦特福德的高比分对决感到惊叹，最终我们以6比4获胜，在U18英超南部联赛中再取三分。
文森特·约瑟夫上演帽子戏法，马利克·哈希梅开二度，阿克塞尔·东切夫也建功立业，帮助我们抵挡了对手的猛烈反扑。
“哇，真是场精彩的比赛。球员和教练组都知道布伦特福德在9场比赛中已经进了33个球，所以我们很清楚他们的威胁。”
“今天真正让人高兴的是，我们在对阵维拉后讨论过把握机会的问题，当时大家都感到很失望。我们创造了很多进攻机会和射门，但进球不够，不过今天我们打进了六个球。”
“然而，我们感到高兴但并不满足。今天有很多本不该丢的球。不过总的来说，还是令人满意的。”
首次代表U18首发出场的约瑟夫抓住机会独中三元，帮助球队击败对手，并受到了称赞。乔什说：“为他感到非常高兴。我认为他在护球、串联和逼抢方面给对手制造了很大麻烦。”
“今天对文尼（约瑟夫）真的很满意。他有个很棒的开局。”
由于周末没有英超2级联赛的比赛，这场伦敦德比为多位常规U21球员提供了在同龄人中出场的宝贵时间。
乔什强调了贯穿我们各级青训营的精神面貌，以及在场上场下将这种心态融入每一个年龄段的重要性。他说：“作为教练组，我们觉得这源于平时的训练。”
“我们有一批小伙子周二踢了U21的比赛，接下来周三还会有一些人代表U19出场。”
“如果我们能在他们回到U18阵容时保持一致的指导方针，我认为这会对他们有很大帮助。”
“我确实觉得，就目前新球员、一年级生和二年级生之间的整体融合而言，本赛季到目前为止是非常积极的。”
乔什回顾了保持高标准以及在整个青训体系中培养顽强态度的重要性，这与我们的男子一线队相呼应。
他还呼吁球员们承担起责任，自己去推动这些标准的提升，同时这支队伍也在不断取得进步。
“过去几周我一直在说，就是要找到这种稳定性，拥有不断前行的坚韧意志。”
“然后我们需要一群能够自我约束、自己去推动标准提升的小伙子，这正是我们一直在推动的。”
“我们觉得他们现在开始迎来转机了。所以关键是要为他们保持高标准，并保持连贯的行为习惯。”

bodyEn: Mikel Arteta used a Spanish word to describe what it felt like to be helpless at Anfield while playing for Everton in 2011: bajar. “It’s when a cyclist is going up and looks amazing, then in one kilometre he goes ‘boom’ and he’s struggling again,” he said in Amazon’s All or Nothing documentary. “The game was going well and then suddenly I could only see red shirts flying around. The game is passing all over me and I cannot react. I only had that feeling in my career once, and it was at Anfield.”

Given Arteta’s record at Liverpool, Sunday’s showdown with his childhood friend Andoni Iraola – five days after Arsenal were dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Fleetwood – could be expected to fill him with dread. Arteta finally tasted victory there as a player with Arsenal in September 2012, after five failed attempts in the Merseyside derby, but ended up spending the night in hospital with concussion after colliding with Jordan Henderson in an incident he has described as “the biggest fear of my life”.

Arteta was part of the Arsenal side that won at Anfield again six months later thanks to goals from the new signings Lukas Podolski and Santi Cazorla. That was the last time the club triumphed there in the Premier League. They have not won at Anfield for 13 league matches, equalling the club’s worst run at Liverpool. Arsenal’s one victory at Liverpool in the interim came in the League Cup on penalties in 2020 on Arteta’s second visit as a manager.

The Spaniard tried to prepare his players for a trip to Anfield in November 2021 by playing You’ll Never Walk Alone over the training ground speakers but that ended in a 4-0 defeat. He was criticised after last season’s loss in late August, when Dominik Szoboszlai’s late free-kick ended a sequence of three Arsenal draws at Liverpool, for a perceived failure to take off the handbrake, having started Mikel Merino as his No 10. Gary Neville went as far as to say Arsenal lacked “the mentality to go and win big matches at big away grounds”, an assertion that will have hurt Arteta but does have credence: they have not beaten Manchester City in the Premier League at the Etihad since 2015 under Arsène Wenger.

Arteta will be keen to disprove such perceptions, especially after Arsenal struggled so badly against a team 84 places below them in the pyramid in a stadium that holds fewer than 6,000 people. The strikers Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyökeres surprisingly started in tandem at Fleetwood, presumably in an attempt to lighten the load on Martin Ødegaard, although both look badly out of form. Bukayo Saka is out with a thigh injury, there are concerns over Noni Madueke’s ankle and Arsenal’s failed appeal over Max Dowman’s red card rules out the teenager for three matches.

With that in mind, Arteta’s best chance of beating Liverpool is probably by taking the cautious approach that has served him so well and was the cornerstone of last season’s Premier League title triumph. He can take inspiration from one of the most famous nights in Arsenal’s history 37 years ago when George Graham’s side arrived at Anfield needing a 2-0 victory to be champions.

“I told my players to keep things tight in the first half – it was imperative we did not concede,” said Graham in an interview to mark the 20th anniversary of that dramatic finale to the 1988-89 season, when Michael Thomas scored in stoppage time to end Arsenal’s 18-year wait for the title. “The papers were saying we’d have to attack from the off, but I was adamant that was wrong. If Liverpool had scored an early goal it would have been over. But they did very little attacking and played into our hands.”

Before the 1989 game, Arsenal’s players ran to all four corners of the ground to hand flowers to Liverpool fans as a show of sympathy after the Hillsborough disaster the previous month – an idea proposed by their longstanding director Ken Friar, who died this month.

Graham and Arteta were 44 when they won their first league titles and the similarities do not end there. The former Scotland midfielder, who scored almost 80 goals for Arsenal and helped them win the Double in 1971, was known for his emphasis on defending as a manager and “1-0 to the Arsenal” became synonymous with Graham, especially towards the end of his reign. Arteta has revived that tradition since he took over in December 2019, recording 1-0 victories 32 times in the Premier League, more than any club apart from Everton.

Arsenal scored their first set-piece goal of the season in a routine 2-0 win at home to Everton last Saturday and targeting Liverpool’s weakness from set plays while keeping things tight at the other end could be the most effective tactic against a team who have been finding their feet under Iraola in recent weeks.

“Collectively, we acknowledge the importance of defending,” said Arteta last year when asked about comparisons between his team and Graham’s. “We know that if we excel in that part of the game, the chances and the probabilities to win more matches is going to be very, very high.”
Arsenal flew back to London after losing to Fleetwood on penalties in a shootout that will have revived bad memories of May’s Champions League final defeat by Paris Saint-Germain.

The Carabao Cup has stretched Arteta’s squad in the past two seasons, when they reached first the semi-finals then the final, so that is one potential positive from their elimination – not that the ultra-competitive Spaniard would agree. For him, the only way to respond to the most embarrassing night of his managerial career will be to follow in Graham’s footsteps on Sunday.

items.titleZh: 阿尔特塔可从乔治·格拉汉姆身上汲取灵感，抹去安菲尔德的痛苦回忆
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳已在英超客场对阵利物浦13场不胜，阿尔特塔希望效仿前辈格拉汉姆迎来突破。
bodyZh: 米克尔·阿尔特塔曾用一个西班牙语单词来形容2011年效力埃弗顿期间在安菲尔德感到无助时的感受：bajar。“这就像一个骑自行车的人正在爬坡并且表现惊艳，然后在一公里内他突然‘砰’的一声，又开始挣扎了，”他在亚马逊的纪录片《全或无》中说道，“比赛进行得很顺利，然后突然我只能看到红色的球衣在身边飞奔。比赛从我身边掠过，我无法反应。我的职业生涯中只有一次有过这种感觉，那就是在安菲尔德。”
鉴于阿尔特塔在利物浦的战绩，在阿森纳被弗利特伍德淘汰出联赛杯五天后，周日与他童年好友安东尼·伊劳拉的对决可能会让他感到恐惧。在默西塞德郡德比中经历五次失败后，阿尔特塔终于在2012年9月作为阿森纳球员在那里尝到了胜利的滋味，但由于与乔丹·亨德森相撞，他最终因脑震荡在医院度过了一夜，他将这次事件描述为“我一生中最大的恐惧”。
六个月后，凭借新援卢卡斯·波多尔斯基和圣地亚哥·卡索拉的进球，阿尔特塔随阿森纳再次在安菲尔德取胜。那是俱乐部上一次在英超联赛中在那里取胜。他们已经在安菲尔德连续13场联赛未能取胜，追平了俱乐部在利物浦的最差纪录。在此期间，阿森纳在利物浦取得的一场胜利是在2020年联赛杯的点球大战中，这也是阿尔特塔第二次以主教练身份到访。

这位西班牙人曾试图在2021年11月前往安菲尔德前，在训练场的扬声器里播放《你永远不会独行》来为球员做准备，但那场比赛最终以0比4告败。在去年8月下旬失利后，他受到了批评，当时多米尼克·索博斯莱的远射任意球终结了阿森纳在利物浦的三连平，人们认为他没有松开手刹，因为他让米克尔·梅里诺首发出任10号位。加里·内维尔甚至表示阿森纳缺乏“在重要客场赢得重要比赛的心态”，这一言论可能会伤害到阿尔特塔，但确实有其道理：自2015年温格执教以来，他们在英超联赛中从未在阿提哈德球场击败过曼城。
阿尔特塔将渴望打破这种看法，特别是考虑到阿森纳在一个容量不到6000人、且身处低级别联赛84位之遥的球队面前表现得如此挣扎。前锋凯·哈弗茨和维克托·哲凯赖什令人意外地在弗利特伍德联袂首发，这大概是为了减轻马丁·厄德高的负担，尽管两人看起来状态都很糟糕。布卡约·萨卡因大腿受伤缺阵，人们对农尼·马杜埃克的脚踝感到担忧，而阿森纳对马克斯·唐曼红牌的上诉失败也让这名少将面临三场禁赛。
有鉴于此，阿尔特塔击败利物浦的最佳机会可能是采取他擅长的谨慎态度，这也是他上赛季赢得英超冠军的基石。他可以从37年前阿森纳历史上最著名的夜晚之一中汲取灵感，当时乔治·格拉汉姆的球队抵达安菲尔德时，需要一场2-0的胜利才能夺冠。
“我告诉球员们在上半场要保持紧凑——我们绝不能失球，”格拉汉姆在纪念1988-89赛季戏剧性结局20周年的采访中说道，当时迈克尔·托马斯在补时阶段进球，结束了阿森纳长达18年的冠军荒。“报纸上说我们必须从一开始就进攻，但我坚信那是错的。如果利物浦早早进球，比赛就结束了。但他们几乎没有进攻，正合我们心意。”
在1989年的比赛之前，阿森纳球员跑向球场的四个角落，向利物浦球迷献花，以表达对上个月希尔斯堡惨案的同情——这个想法是由他们长期担任总监的肯·弗里尔提出的，他于本月去世。
格拉汉姆和阿尔特塔在赢得他们的第一个联赛冠军时都是44岁，两者的相似之处远不止于此。这位前苏格兰中场曾为阿森纳打入近80球并在1971年帮助他们赢得双冠王，作为主教练，他以强调防守而闻名，“1-0给阿森纳”成为了格拉汉姆的代名词，尤其是在他执教后期。自2019年12月接手以来，阿尔特塔复兴了这一传统，在英超联赛中32次以1-0取胜，除了埃弗顿之外，没有哪家俱乐部比这更多。

上周六，阿森纳在主场2-0轻取埃弗顿，打入了本赛季的第一个定位球，在另一端保持紧凑的同时，针对利物浦在定位球上的弱点，可能是对阵这支最近几周在伊劳拉带领下逐渐找到状态的球队最有效的战术。
“作为一个集体，我们承认防守的重要性，”阿尔特塔去年被问及他的球队与格拉汉姆的球队之间的比较时说道，“我们知道，如果我们能在比赛的那个部分表现出色，赢得更多比赛的机会和概率将会非常非常高。”
在点球大战中负于弗利特伍德后，阿森纳飞回伦敦，这场失利重新唤起了5月份欧冠决赛输给巴黎圣日耳曼的不愉快回忆。
联赛杯在过去两个赛季中拉长了阿尔特塔的阵容，当时他们先是打入半决赛，然后打入决赛，所以这是他们被淘汰带来的一个潜在积极因素——不过这位极具竞争力的西班牙人可不会这么认为。对他来说，回应他执教生涯中最尴尬夜晚的唯一方法，就是周日追随格拉汉姆的脚步。
